chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who recited al-Ḥamd and half of a surah in one rakʿah: would it suffice him in the second that he not recite al-Ḥamd and instead recite what remained of the surah? He said: He should recite al-Ḥamd, then recite what remained of the surah.
So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as applying to supererogatory prayers rather than the obligatory prayers; that is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.سُورَةٍ: a chapter of the Qur'an recited after al-Ḥamd

ai.seo_question: If someone recites half a surah in one rakʿah, should they recite al-Ḥamd again in the next rakʿah before completing the surah?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses recitation in salat when a person has recited only part of a surah in one rakʿah. The Imam عليه السلام states that in the next rakʿah one should recite al-Ḥamd again and then complete the remainder of the surah. The compiler then clarifies that this report is to be understood as concerning supererogatory prayers, not obligatory ones.
